feed.title: Oil tanker incident reported near Red Sea

brief.snapshot: Reported tanker incident near the Red Sea raises immediate concern around commercial shipping security and rerouting risk.
brief.impact: Bullish pressure on crude oil, shipping insurance, maritime security, and gold risk premium; bearish for risk assets if escalation broadens.
brief.scenario_up: Further vessel attacks or carrier rerouting would likely raise freight costs and add an oil-risk premium.
brief.scenario_down: Rapid clarification, no damage, or no follow-on incidents would reduce urgency and keep this as a monitored signal.
brief.action: Monitor closely; avoid chasing after a spike and look for confirmation through shipping flows or insurance/freight pricing.

feed.title: Hormuz traffic remains severely restricted; normal tanker flow not restored

brief.snapshot: Restricted tanker flow through Hormuz would represent a direct threat to global energy logistics.
brief.impact: Strongly bullish crude oil and energy volatility; supportive for gold and bearish for equities if sustained.
brief.scenario_up: If restrictions persist or expand, oil volatility and inflation-risk pricing could rise quickly.
brief.scenario_down: If traffic normalizes within hours, the market may unwind part of the geopolitical premium.
brief.action: Treat as high-priority energy-risk signal; wait for confirmation from shipping traffic and price response before acting.

feed.title: Major energy producer delays regional restart until Strait of Hormuz transit stabilizes

brief.snapshot: A delayed restart indicates the chokepoint issue is affecting real operations, not only sentiment.
brief.impact: Bullish for crude and energy equities if production or export flows remain impaired; possible drag on broad equities through inflation concerns.
brief.scenario_up: Additional producers delaying operations would confirm a broader supply-chain impact.
brief.scenario_down: Restart confirmation would weaken the supply-disruption thesis.
brief.action: Upgrade Hormuz risk monitoring; prioritize confirmation from producer statements and tanker movement.

feed.title: Russian oil output pressured after repeated Ukrainian strikes on ports and refineries

brief.snapshot: Repeated strikes on energy infrastructure can reduce export capacity, refinery throughput, or insurance appetite.
brief.impact: Bullish for crude supply risk and defense/geopolitical risk premium; bearish for European growth if energy stress rises.
brief.scenario_up: More successful strikes or sustained repair delays would strengthen the supply-disruption thesis.
brief.scenario_down: Rapid repairs or unchanged export volumes would reduce market impact.
brief.action: Use as supply-risk context; avoid treating it as actionable without evidence of actual output/export disruption.
